# 三官燈儀

**ID:** KR5a0203
**Custom ID:** ZB5a0203

**Editions:** SJB, ZHDZ

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A short lamp-ritual addressed to the Three Officials (*sānguān* 三官) — Heaven, Earth, and Water — the great judicial-hierarchical triad of early Daoism, dating in cult to the second-century Celestial-Master *sān guān shǒu shū* 三官手書 confession-petition. The rite is set in a Pure Offering (*qīnggòng* 清供) performed for an individual on the days of the Three Principles (*sānyuán* 三元): on the fifteenth of the first, seventh, and tenth lunar months, days on which "the Three Officials correct the accounts and the Nine Heavens grant happiness." Three lamps are lit in turn, each accompanied by a confession of faults addressed to the corresponding Official, and a request for the cancelling of the votary's debts in the celestial registers.

**Abstract**

John Lagerwey, in Schipper & Verellen eds., *The Taoist Canon* (2004) 2:965 (§3.B.1, Zhèngyī, "Lamp Rituals"), describes the work succinctly: "This lamp ritual belongs to a Pure Offering performed for an individual on the days of the Three Principles, on which days 'the Three Officials correct the accounts and the Nine Heavens grant happiness.'" The text follows the standard structural and linguistic pattern of the editorial group DZ 197–214 (the *zhìxīn guīmìng* homage formula and *fúyuàn* statement of wishes), and concludes with the prescribed reading of a memorial (*shū* 疏) and the recitation of a sacred text. On the antiquity of the Sānguān cult — which goes back to the first generation of the Way of the Celestial Masters in the second century — see *[DZ 1411 Mǐngzhēn kē](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a1411)* and the *sān guān shǒu shū* discussed in Stephen Bokenkamp, *Early Daoist Scriptures* (Berkeley 1997). The frontmatter brackets the work 1100–1400, the canonical Sòng–Yuán range of the editorial group.
